rows.grounds: compound of dharma and sāra; describes the essential core of dharma
genitive plural indicating the body of texts to which the essence belongs
metaphor for the innermost core or central teaching
qualifies hṛdayaṃ as the highest or ultimate

items.question: What constitutes the supreme heart and essential dharma of the tantras?
premises: The tantras possess an essential core identified as dharmasāra.
This core is characterized as the hṛdayaṃ of the tantras.
This heart is described as supreme (param).
items.inference: Therefore, the supreme heart of the tantras is their essential dharma.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of dharmasāraṃ and hṛdayaṃ as appositional or predicative is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: It is the essence of dharma, the supreme heart of the tantras.
